Episode 258. The Predator of all Dimensions (20)
Before the footsteps of Ameris and Lokia, the distant sound of explosions was heard first.
As time had begun to flow again, the battle was naturally resuming. No one knew that time had been stopped by the Valeria from another dimension.

The corridor was becoming noisy. With Talaris's grand sealing being lifted sooner than expected, Leuth and the crew had rushed over. Leuth's face was pale, thinking that something had happened to Talaris.
[Lady of the Secret Palace, the seal... no, Y-Young Patriarch!? Your arm, no, Valeria!]
Everyone, unable to understand, stared at Jin and Valeria, who was tied to him. In their perception, the two had been fighting in the Genesis Knights' battlefield until just a moment ago.
The priests who had come with Leuth hastily tried to heal Jin. But Jin waved them away. It was a wound that no one, including Lani, could heal.
"Chief Butler, there's no time, so I'll be brief. Until just a moment ago, the time on the battlefield was stopped for everyone except me, Lady Ameris, and Lokia."
What? Leuth did not ask back. She too, like Talaris, quickly grasped the situation. Whatever it was, if the Young Patriarch was here now, there had to be a good reason.
[I'm listening.]

"The Valeria from another world helped. Thanks to her, the curse on Temar's left arm has been lifted now. So from now on, I will enter the sanctuary. Praying... that there is something there that will end this war."
What was he praying to? Not a god. It was the people. It was a prayer directed towards the people fighting alongside him.
[Understood. I will prepare whatever you command.]
Soon, Jin stepped inside the workshop.

Ameris and Lokia were gasping for breath next to the coffin where Temar's arm lay. Both were exhausted to their limits from releasing the curse so quickly. Lokia, in particular, was in a state where her face and body were rotting and festering. As if the past thousand years had suddenly blown over her.
"...I thought for sure you would betray us and we'd have one more useless fight, but I guess that won't be happening."
It was clear.

Lokia was now in a state no different from an old, powerless witch one could easily find in a common story. Her black nails, soaked in long-standing madness and evil, looked as if they would fall off at the slightest touch, and so did her yellowed teeth.
Lokia had initially told Leuth to restrain her if she couldn't be trusted. That helping with the curse removal would not be a problem with even a minimal amount of magic.
If Leuth had restrained Lokia then, she wouldn't have even had her rotten body left now. Lokia had entered the workshop from the beginning, prepared for annihilation.
Soon, with her powerless eyes buried in wrinkles, she looked back and forth between Jin's left arm and Temar's left arm placed beside it.
"Puhuhu... you really came with your left arm lost... The world loves you to an annoying degree, descendant. I'm really getting jealous."
"Your sacrifice now does not justify your betrayal."
"I was merely struggling."
"What you have done for the past thousand years was not a struggle, but scheming and manipulation. Did you see the Zipples as those who struggle? You are the same."
The moment Jin was about to pick up Temar's left arm, Lokia cackled again and opened her mouth.

"Yes, yes, you may not be wrong. But how do you plan to use that? To enter the legacy, you must wield Barisada with Temar's body. Only then will the barrier be lifted. Surely you're not going to forcibly tie Barisada to that arm and then grab that arm with your right arm to swing it? That would be quite a sight!"

Grab! Lokia grabbed Jin's waist. With more than half of her body melted like a swamp, grabbing his waist was the limit no matter how she stretched her hand. The moment he tried to pull her away, Lokia cackled again.

"Here, try attaching it to your arm. I added one more function while releasing the curse. For some reason, I felt it would turn out like this. For some reason, I felt it would... turn out like this..."
Jin didn't answer and looked at Ameris. When Ameris nodded, Jin without hesitation brought Temar's left arm to his own left shoulder.
Ssssss... tzzzzzt...!

A soft scraping sound, like a spring being wound, arose, and thin strings of magic were seen forming between the wound and Temar's left arm. The thousands of thread-like magic strands connected Jin's shoulder and Temar's arm as if they were one body in less than ten seconds.
Jin felt a sensation of a thick, surging energy from his left arm spreading throughout his entire body.

The true energy of Temar that remained in his left arm had spread. Though it couldn't be called the complete true energy of a Genesis Knight's arm, having been tormented by all sorts of curses and experiments for a thousand years, there was no other means to restore Jin more than this at the moment.
"Hahaha...! As expected, it suits you well. It's the final gift from your failed ancestor. Use it well and don't lose it..."
Hssss… chhh! Lokia's breathing became sharp. Annihilation was approaching.
"Chief Butler."
Only then did Jin release Valeria from his body. Was it because his true energy had been restored? Valeria, who had been so heavy, was transferred from Jin's arms to Leuth as lightly as a lie.

Leuth, who received Valeria, said nothing about her. The descendant of the fairy race, a Hister, the last survivor, who had been lonely and desolate her whole life, who had finally found a place to rest her heart, a kin.

But on this battlefield, there were not just one or two who had fought so lonely and died. Jin had been forced to hold Valeria all along to defeat his enemies, but Leuth was different. She could not treat Valeria as special. No matter how much he wanted to.
"I'm going."
With every second that passed, the offensive of Kelliark and the Demon Army was intensifying. Right now, Lafrarosa was being relentlessly shattered and shaken by the merciless bombardment of the sun.

But Jin was no longer just afraid of Kelliark, of people dying by his power. Of course he was afraid, but if the legacy truly held something that could defeat him, he might be able to shove a sword into his neck. He might finally be able to slaughter the mad monster who called himself the one true god.

'Kelliark, you should have finished us before I got this. You should have killed every single one. But you couldn't, even with that great power. I've found the path, all that's left is for me to obtain the legacy. Which means... it's my turn.'
It wasn't just true energy that remained in Temar's left arm.

A kind of 'authentication' set by Solderet a thousand years ago was manifesting, and the exact location of the legacy was also being transmitted to his mind. The authenticator was Jin Runcandel, and the location of the legacy was in the territory of Morganiel in the Black Sea. Even though it was covered by the red sea, Jin could now recognize it at a glance.
[Yes, good luck... Go and seize it. Grasp it! Show them that at the end of the struggle, it is we who stand last.]
As Leuth knelt on one knee to show her respects, everyone nearby offered a sword salute. Even those who were not vassals of Runcandel all showed the highest form of respect they could.

"Jin, you owe me a lot. You'll never be able to repay it, no matter what you do. But if you come back alive this time, if you defeat them... I'll consider it all received. I'll think you've paid back everything, including the interest... You are a person who always repays a kindness. A person who doesn't forget. So you will definitely come back."
Talaris briefly embraced Jin. From between the wrinkles around her eyes, a teardrop, shining like a snowflake, flowed down.
Jin left. He ran down the corridor with all his might and threw himself straight out of the bridge.
It was time for the others to leave as well. Talaris planned to go to the ground after recovering for a short while, and Ameris likewise.
Leuth had to return to the bridge and lead Lafrarosa, which was collapsing under the sun. The first sight the Young Patriarch saw upon his return could not be a destroyed and fallen Lafrarosa.
"Heh heh... kuh... Leuth..."

[Is there still more you have to say? Traitor. You will not be able to see with your own two eyes the Young Patriarch cutting down the Zipples, the moment Runcandel finally shines brightest in its thousand-year history. An ending where you are ultimately not saved, are you satisfied? Your twisted final affection for the family was, nevertheless, meaningful. But that's all.]

Leuth intended to leave Lokia to die on her own and quickly go to the bridge. The friendship from a thousand years ago when they fought together and the current sense of betrayal inevitably intersected dizzily for a moment. But that didn't mean she felt a sliver of sympathy.
"Listen... it's about... our niece."
At those words, a flame sparked in Leuth's eyes.
[What did you say? Our? Our? Haylin is not your niece!]
Lokia took something out from her bosom with a trembling hand. It was an orb so clear that it was hard to believe it was something Lokia possessed.

"Haylin... puhuhu, that child's body is alive. To be precise, it was alive. It seems to have been absorbed by Kelliark, who has obtained the Sun God's power now... but anyway, this is Haylin's soul, separated from Araxion."
[...Haylin's?]
"I was going to show her. This child."
Lokia Ganesto.

For the past thousand years, she had been searching for a way to 'revert' the world. After reverting the world to a state with no light, no darkness, and no matter, she intended to fill that empty space with the land she had created.
And when that time came, Lokia intended to show Haylin's soul that world. The scenery of the 'just' world she had created as the price for her thousand-year betrayal.
In a way, to Lokia, Haylin's soul was the last greed she had as a Runcandel.

It was the reason why she had painstakingly separated Haylin's soul over hundreds of years, even though it was of no help to her ultimate goal. We may not see it, but our child will be able to see a world where Runcandel is victorious.
Lokia did not explain the details to Leuth. It was a story no one could understand anyway. In fact, even she herself didn't understand it.
"Give it to Lucy... If by any chance, if by any chance Jin Runcandel defeats the Zipples, she'll be able to see it. Haylin, too."
Leuth had already taken the orb as if snatching it and was walking away. It was because she couldn't listen to Lokia's words any longer.
"Heh heh."
Lokia thought for the last time of the members of Ganesto who had died fighting on the battlefield. Ran, Vyugo, Myu, Anne, and Joshua.

They were children who could never be satisfactory as the price for a thousand-year betrayal. They were children she could not love in the slightest. From the beginning, to Lokia, they were nothing more than expendable items she had to use for lack of a better option.

But for some reason, she was thinking of them now. She was wishing they were by her side. But the knights of Ganesto had all already met a miserable end on the battlefield. Even Joshua, who had merged with Iloanu.
"...It's the end."
Thus, the House of Ganesto disappeared from the world.
